text:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH - GPU fleet ECC/Xid spike detected in prod-gpu-pool (node-05). Metric: correctable_ecc_errors > 50/min. Auto-escalation to oncall.
oncall-bot: @morgan you're on call — please ack and triage :rotating_light:
morgan: ACK. I'm digging in. grabbing logs and checking node health.
ivan: I see `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 62, pid=32011` repeats in dmesg for node-05. Also kernel shows `gpu reset successful` twice then OOMs for a couple of containers.
sara: tagging infra team. @jules can you check rack power/thermal telemetry? might be temperature-related.
jules: thermal looks nominal. inlet temps 27C. no fan ramps. I'm more suspicious of a driver/kernel regression after last rollout.
morgan: copying key logs here:
```
Mar 09 14:03:21 node-05 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 62, pid=32011, GPU has fallen off the bus.
Mar 09 14:03:22 node-05 dockerd: containerd: oom-kill: Killed process 32011 (infer_runtime) total-vm:12000000kB
```
morgan: impact check — prometheus shows 4% of inferences in us-west-2 returning 503s, mostly routed through node-05. Several customer jobs failed with container restarts.
nate: creating ops bridge and support ticket. link: https://ops.example.com/bridge/BR-10823
ops-bridge-bot: Bridge created: BR-10823 — invite stakeholder group `#support-bridge` and `customer-ops`.
customer-ops: joined. Notifying affected customers with a short heads-up: "We're investigating increased GPU driver resets affecting a subset of nodes; may see transient 5xxs. We'll update ASAP." I'll post an ETA when we have a mitigation.
morgan: plan: 1) cordon node-05 2) drain pods with `--delete-local-data --ignore-daemonsets` 3) attempt `systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced` and `modprobe -r nvidia && modprobe nvidia` if safe 4) if resets continue, evacuate node and set it to quarantine via fleet tag.
ivan: agreed. Also collect `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,UTILIZATION` output and `/var/log/nvidia-installer.log`.
ivan: running quick check: `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY` shows ECC correctable errors incrementing every 10s.
sara: rolling a small canary to fallback: switching 10% of traffic off prod-gpu-pool to dedicated-capacity-usw to reduce pressure.
jules: started drain: `kubectl drain node-05 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` — some pods stuck in Terminating due to preStop hooks.
morgan: forcing eviction for stuck containers:
```
kubectl patch pod <pod> -n inference --type=json -p='[{"op":"remove","path":"/metadata/finalizers"}]'
```
morgan: after eviction, node shows `NVRM: GPU fell off bus` even after driver reload. I'm seeing periodic `Xid 13` now too.
ivan: looks like ECC errors propagate to multiple GPUs on the node. recommend full evacuation and quarantine.
ops-bridge-bot: Quarantine tag applied to node-05: `evacuated=true, quarantine=driver-reset-spike` — autoscaler notified.
morgan: taking node-05 out of rotation in the router: `rbacctl set-weight node-05 0` and marking as `no-sched` in fleet.
nate: proactively spinning up two replacement nodes in prod-gpu-pool to maintain capacity.
sara: monitoring: error rate dropped from 4% to 0.5% after traffic shift. still seeing isolated retries.
morgan: root cause hypothesis: GPU driver experiencing latent ECC-correctable queue overflow leading to Xid propagation and eventually driver resets; could be exacerbated by a recent kernel patch.
jules: collecting kernel/driver package versions: `kernel 6.2.18`, `nvidia-driver 530.41.03` — cross-referencing with release notes.
ivan: also found `oom-kill` inside `infer_runtime` repeatedly — might be the app not handling transient GPU disappearances.
customer-ops: drafting customer note: "We observed transient GPU driver resets in a small subset of nodes causing brief 5xxs between 14:03–14:20 UTC. Mitigation: traffic reroute and node quarantine. No data loss; jobs restarted automatically. Follow-up: preventive quarantine and driver rollback investigation."
customer-ops: sending to legal/ops for review before publish.
morgan: next steps: run overnight soak on driver 525.x candidate on a quarantine node to see if regression is in 530.x, collect extended ECC telemetry, and create an alert to trigger earlier when correctable errors per GPU > 10/min (current is 50/min threshold).
ivan: dumping NVSMI logs and gdb backtrace for `infer_runtime` process: attaching to bridge.
nate: capacity update — dedicated-capacity-usw picking up surplus load, no customers blocked now.
ops-bridge-bot: Summary created in BR-10823: actions taken, nodes quarantined, customers notified, next steps — link appended to incident timeline.
morgan: closing the active pager for node-05 now. We'll keep bridge open for postmortem. Please add any notes you saw during the window.
sara: note: saw a single other node (node-12) show a tiny bump in ECC but it stabilized — likely same class but not triggering resets.
jules: I've scheduled a follow-up maintenance window to try driver rollback and deeper hardware tests.
customer-ops: posted the customer-facing update at 14:45 UTC.
ivan: grabbing ASQ logs and will upload to BR-10823.
morgan: thanks all. reassigning postmortem owner to @ivan. Closing thread but keep watch overnight.
incident-bot: Pager cleared for node-05 at 14:20 UTC. Follow-up priority: HIGH — postmortem required.
